q_location.question: Where exactly is the pain located?

q_onset.question: Did the pain start suddenly or gradually?

q_radiating.question: Is the pain spreading to your arm, shoulder, jaw, neck, or back?

q_symptoms.question: Are you experiencing any of these symptoms?

res_chest_emergency.title: 🚨 EMERGENCY MEDICAL WARNING
res_chest_emergency.message: ⚠️ This combination of symptoms can be serious and needs urgent medical evaluation.
res_chest_emergency.warning: Chest pain accompanied by radiating pain, breathlessness, sweating, or dizziness may indicate a critical cardiac emergency. Please call emergency services (112) immediately.
guidance: Call emergency services (112) immediately.
Stop all physical activity immediately.
Sit or rest in a comfortable position (leaning back with knees slightly bent).
Loosen any tight clothing around neck and chest.
Do NOT drive yourself to the hospital.
Follow instructions from emergency medical professionals.

res_chest_urgent.title: ⚠️ URGENT MEDICAL EVALUATION RECOMMENDED
res_chest_urgent.message: Chest pain (especially on the left side or radiating) should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.
res_chest_urgent.warning: Although immediate red-flag symptoms were not reported, localized or radiating chest pain requires prompt medical evaluation.
guidance: Rest quietly and avoid any strenuous activity.
Have someone escort you to an urgent care center or hospital emergency room.
If pain worsens or breathlessness/sweating develops, call 112 immediately.

res_chest_low.title: 📋 FIRST-AID & MONITORING GUIDANCE
res_chest_low.warning: This pain may be related to muscle strain or mild irritation. Monitor your symptoms closely.
guidance: Rest in a comfortable position.
Avoid heavy lifting or torso twisting.
Practice calm, steady breathing.
If symptoms persist or worsen, consult a doctor.

q_responsive.question: Is the person conscious and responsive to firm shoulder tapping and shouting?

q_breathing_conscious.question: Are they breathing normally or experiencing chest discomfort?

q_breathing_unconscious.question: Check breathing for 10 seconds: Is the person breathing normally?

res_cpr_emergency.title: 🚨 CRITICAL CARDIAC ARREST EMERGENCY
res_cpr_emergency.message: ⚠️ Person is unresponsive and not breathing normally! Immediate CPR required.
res_cpr_emergency.warning: This is a life-threatening emergency. Call 112 immediately and begin CPR compressions.
guidance: Call 112 (or local emergency services) immediately and fetch an AED if available.
Position the person flat on their back on a firm surface.
Place heel of one hand in center of chest; interlock fingers of other hand.
Push hard and fast: 100 to 120 compressions per minute (2 inches / 5 cm deep).
Allow full chest recoil after each push.
If trained, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 compressions; otherwise perform continuous hands-only CPR.
Continue until paramedics arrive or AED is ready.

res_cpr_recovery_position.title: ⚠️ UNCONSCIOUS BUT BREATHING
res_cpr_recovery_position.message: Person is unresponsive but breathing normally.
res_cpr_recovery_position.warning: Unconsciousness requires medical evaluation. Place in recovery position to protect airway.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Roll the person onto their side into the recovery position.
Tilt head back gently to keep airway open and clear.
Monitor breathing continuously until paramedics arrive.

res_cpr_urgent.title: ⚠️ URGENT MEDICAL CARE REQUIRED
res_cpr_urgent.message: Conscious person with severe respiratory or cardiac discomfort.
res_cpr_urgent.warning: Requires prompt medical evaluation to prevent cardiac deterioration.
guidance: Keep the person seated comfortably and quiet.
Loosen tight clothing around neck and chest.
Call 112 if symptoms escalate or consciousness decreases.

res_cpr_monitor.title: 📋 STABLE - MONITOR RESPONSIVENESS
res_cpr_monitor.message: Person is conscious and breathing normally.
res_cpr_monitor.warning: Monitor for any changes in condition.
guidance: Ensure person remains seated or resting.
Offer water if alert and oriented.
Seek medical advice if feeling unwell.

q_speak_cough.question: Is the person able to speak or cough?

res_choking_cough_guidance.title: 📋 MILD AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION
res_choking_cough_guidance.warning: Do not interfere with natural coughing. Encourage them to keep coughing.
guidance: Encourage the person to keep coughing forcefully.
Stay with them and monitor closely.
Do NOT give back blows while they are coughing strongly on their own.

res_choking_conscious_guidance.title: 🚨 SEVERE CHOKING EMERGENCY
res_choking_conscious_guidance.message: ⚠️ Complete airway blockage! Immediate intervention needed.
res_choking_conscious_guidance.warning: Person cannot breathe or speak. Act immediately and call emergency services (112).
guidance: Call 112 immediately or ask someone nearby to call.
Give 5 firm back blows: Lean person forward and strike firmly between shoulder blades with heel of hand.
If back blows fail, give 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver): Stand behind, wrap arms around waist, make a fist above navel, pull inward and upward sharply.
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until object is dislodged.

res_choking_unconscious_guidance.title: 🚨 UNCONSCIOUS CHOKING EMERGENCY
res_choking_unconscious_guidance.message: ⚠️ Person has lost consciousness due to airway blockage!
res_choking_unconscious_guidance.warning: Call 112 immediately and begin CPR compressions.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Lower the person carefully onto their back on the floor.
Begin CPR chest compressions (30 compressions).
Before rescue breaths, open mouth and remove object ONLY if visibly seen.
Continue CPR until emergency responders take over.

q_heavy.question: Is the bleeding heavy or spurting?

q_pressure.question: Is blood continuing to flow despite firm direct pressure?

res_bleeding_emergency.title: 🚨 SEVERE HEMORRHAGE EMERGENCY
res_bleeding_emergency.message: ⚠️ Severe bleeding can lead to life-threatening shock within minutes.
res_bleeding_emergency.warning: Uncontrolled bleeding requires urgent emergency dispatch and hard direct pressure. Call 112 immediately.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Apply firm, continuous direct pressure on the wound using a clean cloth, sterile dressing, or gloved hand.
Do NOT release pressure to check the wound.
If blood soaks through, add more cloths on top and compress harder.
If severe limb bleeding persists, apply a tourniquet 2-3 inches above the wound if trained.
Keep the person lying down and warm to prevent shock.

res_bleeding_moderate.title: ⚠️ MODERATE BLEEDING CONTROL
res_bleeding_moderate.warning: Ensure clean pressure dressing and check if stitches are required.
guidance: Maintain steady direct pressure for 10 minutes.
Clean around the wound gently once bleeding slows.
Apply a sterile bandage or dressing.
Seek medical evaluation if wound is deep or edges gap open.

q_body_part.question: Which part of the body is affected?

q_blisters.question: Does the burn have blisters, charred skin, or cover a large area?

res_burn_chemical_emergency.title: 🚨 CHEMICAL BURN EMERGENCY
res_burn_chemical_emergency.message: ⚠️ Chemical burns can continue damaging skin until thoroughly flushed.
res_burn_chemical_emergency.warning: Flush with clean water immediately and call 112.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Flush the affected area continuously with cool tap water for at least 20 minutes.
Remove contaminated clothing while flushing.
Do NOT apply ice, butter, or ointments.

res_burn_electrical_emergency.title: 🚨 ELECTRICAL BURN EMERGENCY
res_burn_electrical_emergency.message: ⚠️ Electrical burns can cause internal tissue damage.
guidance: Ensure power source is disconnected safely.
Call 112 immediately.
Check breathing and pulse.
Cover burn entry/exit wounds loosely with sterile dry dressings.

res_burn_facial_emergency.title: 🚨 FACIAL / AIRWAY BURN EMERGENCY
res_burn_facial_emergency.message: ⚠️ Burns to face or neck can cause rapid airway swelling.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Keep person sitting upright to assist breathing.
Apply cool wet compresses gently without blocking airway.

res_burn_severe.title: ⚠️ SEVERE / BLISTERED BURN CARE
res_burn_severe.message: Second or third-degree burn requiring medical treatment.
guidance: Cool burn under running tap water for 10-20 minutes.
Cover loosely with sterile non-stick bandage or plastic wrap.
Do NOT pop blisters or peel burned skin.
Seek medical care at urgent care or emergency room.

res_burn_minor.title: 📋 FIRST-DEGREE MINOR BURN CARE
res_burn_minor.warning: Cool the burn and soothe the skin.
guidance: Cool burn under cool running tap water for 10 minutes.
Apply aloe vera gel or soothing lotion once cooled.
Protect skin from further friction or heat.

q_body_part.question: Which body part may be injured?

q_movement.question: Can the person move the injured area or bear weight?

options.label: Yes - can move with mild pain
Severe pain when trying to move

q_deformity.question: Is there severe swelling, visible deformity, or bone piercing the skin?

q_cause.question: Was the injury caused by a serious accident or fall from height?

res_fracture_spine_emergency.title: 🚨 SUSPECTED SPINAL / HEAD TRAUMA EMERGENCY
res_fracture_spine_emergency.message: ⚠️ Do NOT move the person! Risk of permanent spinal cord injury.
res_fracture_spine_emergency.warning: Call 112 immediately and keep the person completely still.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Do NOT move the person unless there is immediate physical danger (fire/explosion).
Hold head and neck in alignment manually to prevent any movement.
Keep person calm and warm until paramedics arrive.

res_fracture_open_emergency.title: 🚨 OPEN FRACTURE EMERGENCY
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Control bleeding by applying pressure AROUND the bone, not directly on it.
Do NOT try to push the bone back in.
Cover wound loosely with sterile dressing.
Immobilize the limb in position found.

res_fracture_deformed_emergency.title: ⚠️ SUSPECTED CLOSED FRACTURE / DEFORMITY
res_fracture_deformed_emergency.warning: Requires urgent hospital X-ray and splinting.
guidance: Immobilize injured limb using splint or padding.
Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth to reduce swelling.
Transport safely to hospital emergency room or call 112.

res_fracture_urgent.title: ⚠️ HIGH-IMPACT INJURY EVALUATION
res_fracture_urgent.message: High-impact injury with suspected fracture or sprain.
guidance: Rest the limb completely.
Apply ice pack for 15-20 minutes.
Visit emergency room or urgent care clinic for X-ray.

res_fracture_low.title: 📋 MINOR BONE / JOINT DISCOMFORT
res_fracture_low.message: Minor trauma without obvious fracture signs.
res_fracture_low.warning: Monitor for swelling or increasing pain.
guidance: Rest and elevate injured area.
Apply cold compress.
Seek medical advice if unable to use limb.

q_fainted_recently.question: How long did the fainting episode last?

q_symptoms.question: Did they faint with chest pain, numbness, or hit their head during the fall?

options.label: Yes - chest pain / head hit / numbness

res_fainting_unconscious_emergency.title: 🚨 PROLONGED UNCONSCIOUSNESS EMERGENCY
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Check airway and breathing.
If breathing normally, place in recovery position on side.
If not breathing normally, begin CPR compressions immediately.

res_fainting_breathing_emergency.title: 🚨 RESPIRATORY DISTRESS FAINTING EMERGENCY
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Keep airway open and monitor breathing closely.

res_fainting_prolonged_emergency.title: ⚠️ PROLONGED FAINTING EVALUATION
res_fainting_prolonged_emergency.message: Loss of consciousness lasted over 1 minute.
guidance: Keep person lying flat with legs elevated 12 inches.
Do NOT stand up quickly.
Seek medical evaluation at hospital or urgent care.

res_fainting_symptom_emergency.title: ⚠️ FAINTING WITH ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS
res_fainting_symptom_emergency.message: Fainting combined with head impact or cardiac symptoms.
guidance: Keep person resting comfortably.
Check for head injuries or contusions.
Seek emergency medical evaluation.

res_fainting_recovery_guidance.title: 📋 SIMPLE FAINTING RECOVERY CARE
res_fainting_recovery_guidance.message: Brief fainting episode with full recovery.
guidance: Keep lying flat on back with legs elevated for 10 minutes.
Loosen tight clothing around neck.
Offer sips of cool water once fully alert.
Stand up slowly in stages.

q_active.question: Is the person currently having an active seizure / shaking?

q_duration.question: How long has the seizure lasted?

q_repeat_pregnant.question: Is this a second seizure, or is the person pregnant, diabetic, or injured during a fall?

options.label: No - first single seizure / no injury

res_seizure_prolonged_emergency.title: 🚨 STATUS EPILEPTICUS / PROLONGED SEIZURE EMERGENCY
res_seizure_prolonged_emergency.message: ⚠️ Seizure lasting over 5 minutes is a critical emergency!
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Protect head with folded jacket or soft cushion.
Clear surrounding area of hard/sharp objects.
Do NOT restrain movements or put anything in their mouth.

res_seizure_high_risk_emergency.title: 🚨 HIGH-RISK SEIZURE EMERGENCY
res_seizure_high_risk_emergency.message: ⚠️ Repeated seizure or high-risk medical condition.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Roll onto side (recovery position) once shaking stops to keep airway clear.
Reassure person as they wake up.

res_seizure_post_care_guidance.title: ⚠️ SEIZURE POST-CARE GUIDANCE
res_seizure_post_care_guidance.warning: Ensure safe recovery and medical checkup.
guidance: Turn person onto their side into recovery position.
Do NOT put anything in their mouth.
Stay until fully conscious and alert.
Consult a physician or neurologist.

q_contact.question: Is the person still in contact with the live electrical source?

res_electric_touch_warning.title: 🚨 CRITICAL HAZARD: DO NOT TOUCH VICTIM
res_electric_touch_warning.message: ⚠️ Do NOT touch the person until power is safely shut off!
res_electric_touch_warning.warning: Touching a victim in active contact with electricity can electrocute you too.
guidance: Do NOT touch the victim directly.
Turn off main circuit breaker or unplug appliance safely.
If power cannot be cut, use a dry wooden broom handle or rubber object to push wire away.
Call 112 immediately.

res_electric_cpr_emergency.title: 🚨 ELECTRIC SHOCK CARDIAC ARREST EMERGENCY
res_electric_cpr_emergency.message: ⚠️ Person is unresponsive and not breathing normally!
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Begin CPR compressions hard and fast in center of chest.
Continue until emergency medical services arrive.

res_electric_urgent_eval.title: ⚠️ ELECTRIC SHOCK MEDICAL EVALUATION
res_electric_urgent_eval.message: Electric shock recipient requires medical checkup.
res_electric_urgent_eval.warning: All electrical shocks require medical examination for internal cardiac or muscular damage.
guidance: Cool any visible entry/exit burn wounds with cool water.
Cover wounds loosely with sterile dry dressings.
Go to emergency room for ECG and monitoring.

q_symptoms.question: Are they experiencing difficulty breathing, extreme drowsiness, or severe vomiting?

res_poison_unconscious_emergency.title: 🚨 UNCONSCIOUS POISONING EMERGENCY
res_poison_unconscious_emergency.message: ⚠️ Person is unresponsive after toxic substance contact!
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Place in recovery position on side to prevent choking if vomiting occurs.
Do NOT induce vomiting.
Save chemical container or medicine bottle for paramedics.

res_poison_severe_emergency.title: 🚨 SEVERE POISONING EMERGENCY
res_poison_severe_emergency.warning: Call emergency services (112) or Poison Control immediately.
guidance: Call 112 or local Poison Control immediately.
Do NOT induce vomiting unless specifically instructed by experts.
If chemical on skin/eyes, flush with water for 15-20 minutes.
Keep substance container ready for medical team.

res_poison_guidance.title: ⚠️ POISON CONTROL ADVICE REQUIRED
res_poison_guidance.warning: Contact Poison Control center or emergency services promptly.
guidance: Contact Poison Control center or emergency line immediately.
Do NOT give raw egg, salt water, or induce vomiting.
Rinse mouth with clear water if corrosive chemical ingested.

q_duration.question: Has the person been in extreme heat for a prolonged period without fluids?

res_heatstroke_emergency.title: 🚨 CRITICAL HEAT STROKE EMERGENCY
res_heatstroke_emergency.message: ⚠️ High body temperature with altered mental state is life-threatening!
res_heatstroke_emergency.warning: Heat stroke can damage brain and organs. Rapid cooling is mandatory. Call 112.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Move person to cool, shaded or air-conditioned space.
Rapidly cool: Sponge skin with cool water, apply ice packs to armpits, neck, and groin.
Fan continuously while keeping skin wet.
Do NOT give ice-cold drinks rapidly.

res_heat_exhaustion_urgent.title: ⚠️ HEAT EXHAUSTION CARE
res_heat_exhaustion_urgent.warning: Cool body and hydrate to prevent progression to heat stroke.
guidance: Rest in cool shade.
Sip cool electrolyte drink or water.
Loosen tight clothing.
Seek medical care if no improvement after 30 minutes.

res_heat_exhaustion_low.title: 📋 MILD HEAT DISCOMFORT
guidance: Drink fresh cool water.
Rest in air-conditioned room.
Avoid outdoor sunlight until recovered.

q_duration.question: Has the bleeding continued for more than 20 minutes?

q_injured.question: Was the nose injured in a head trauma or violent impact?

q_heavy.question: Is the bleeding very heavy or causing lightheadedness?

res_nosebleed_prolonged_urgent.title: ⚠️ PROLONGED NOSEBLEED EVALUATION
res_nosebleed_prolonged_urgent.warning: Requires medical cautery or packing at urgent care.
guidance: Maintain continuous pinch pressure for another 10 minutes while traveling to medical care.
Sit upright leaning slightly forward.
Visit emergency room or ENT clinic.

res_nosebleed_trauma_urgent.title: ⚠️ TRAUMATIC NOSEBLEED EVALUATION
res_nosebleed_trauma_urgent.warning: Evaluate for nasal fracture or head trauma.
guidance: Lean forward and pinch soft part of nose.
Apply ice pack over bridge of nose.
Seek hospital medical evaluation.

res_nosebleed_heavy_urgent.title: ⚠️ HEAVY NOSEBLEED CARE
res_nosebleed_heavy_urgent.warning: Monitor for dizziness and seek medical aid if persistent.
guidance: Pinch soft lower part of nose firmly for 15 minutes without releasing.
Lean forward, do NOT tilt head back.
Spit out blood instead of swallowing.

res_nosebleed_standard_guidance.title: 📋 STANDARD NOSEBLEED FIRST-AID
guidance: Sit upright and lean forward slightly.
Pinch soft nostrils firmly for 10-15 minutes continuously.
Breathe through mouth.
Avoid blowing nose for several hours after bleeding stops.

options.label: Swelling of face, lips, or tongue

q_hives_extent.question: Are the hives spreading rapidly with any feeling of dizziness or stomach cramps?

res_allergy_anaphylaxis_emergency.title: 🚨 ANAPHYLACTIC SHOCK EMERGENCY
res_allergy_anaphylaxis_emergency.warning: Anaphylaxis requires immediate epinephrine injection and 112 emergency call.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Administer Epinephrine Auto-Injector (EpiPen) into outer thigh if available.
Lay person flat on back (or sit up if breathing is difficult).
Do NOT give oral pills if person has trouble swallowing.
Stay with person until paramedics arrive.

res_allergy_moderate.title: ⚠️ MODERATE ALLERGIC HIVES
guidance: Take over-the-counter antihistamine (cetirizine / diphenhydramine).
Apply cool wet compresses to itchy skin.
Call 112 immediately if throat tightness or lip swelling develops.

res_allergy_mild.title: 📋 MILD ALLERGY CARE
guidance: Wash skin area with mild soap and water.
Take antihistamine if needed.
Rest comfortably.

q_weight.question: Can the person put weight on or move the joint?

q_deformity.question: Is there severe swelling, bruising, or visible joint deformity?

res_sprain_severe_urgent.title: ⚠️ SEVERE SPRAIN / POSSIBLE FRACTURE
res_sprain_severe_urgent.message: Inability to bear weight or severe joint deformation.
guidance: Do NOT force weight bearing on injured joint.
Apply R.I.C.E protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
Visit urgent care for medical evaluation.

res_sprain_rice_guidance.title: 📋 MILD SPRAIN R.I.C.E. CARE
res_sprain_rice_guidance.warning: Follow the R.I.C.E protocol for 48 hours.
guidance: Rest: Avoid putting weight on joint.
Ice: Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15-20 minutes every 2 hours.
Compression: Wrap elastic crepe bandage gently.
Elevation: Prop joint above heart level.

q_deep.question: Is the wound deep or gaping open?

q_dirty.question: Was the wound caused by a dirty/rusty object, animal bite, or is an object stuck in it?

options.label: No - clean glass / paper cut / clean knife

res_cut_heavy_emergency.title: 🚨 SEVERE BLEEDING WOUND EMERGENCY
res_cut_heavy_emergency.message: ⚠️ Heavy wound bleeding requires emergency care!
res_cut_heavy_emergency.warning: Call 112 immediately and press hard on wound.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Apply firm, continuous direct pressure with sterile pad.
Do NOT remove embedded objects—pad around them.

res_cut_gaping_urgent.title: ⚠️ DEEP WOUND EVALUATION (STITCHES)
res_cut_gaping_urgent.warning: Requires professional medical closure (stitches/sutures) within 6-8 hours.
guidance: Apply direct pressure to stop bleeding.
Rinse gently with clean tap water.
Visit urgent care center for stitches.

res_cut_dirty_urgent.title: ⚠️ CONTAMINATED WOUND CARE (TETANUS RISK)
res_cut_dirty_urgent.message: Wound with infection or tetanus risk.
res_cut_dirty_urgent.warning: Requires clinical cleaning and potential tetanus booster.
guidance: Flush thoroughly under cool tap water for 5 minutes.
Do NOT remove deeply embedded objects yourself.
Consult a doctor within 24 hours.

res_cut_minor_guidance.title: 📋 MINOR CUT FIRST-AID
res_cut_minor_guidance.warning: Clean and dress to prevent infection.
guidance: Wash hands before touching wound.
Rinse cut thoroughly under cool tap water.
Apply mild antiseptic ointment.
Cover with clean adhesive bandage.

options.label: Pale, cold, clammy skin with rapid breathing
Weak rapid pulse, confusion, bluish lips

res_shock_emergency.title: 🚨 MEDICAL SHOCK EMERGENCY
res_shock_emergency.message: ⚠️ Circulatory shock is a life-threatening medical emergency!
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Lay person flat on back.
Elevate legs 12 inches (30 cm) unless head, neck, or leg injury is suspected.
Keep person warm with blanket.
Do NOT give food or water.

res_shock_moderate.title: ⚠️ PRE-SHOCK / DEHYDRATION EVALUATION
res_shock_moderate.message: Signs of mild circulatory distress or dizziness.
guidance: Lie flat and rest quietly.
Loosen tight clothing.
Call 112 if skin becomes cold/clammy or confusion develops.

q_headache_type.question: What type of headache symptoms are you or the person experiencing?

options.label: Sudden severe 'thunderclap' pain, stiff neck, or high fever
Throbbing pain on one side with light/sound sensitivity or nausea
Dull aching pressure like a tight band around forehead/neck
Severe sharp piercing pain around one eye with tearing
Facial pressure around cheeks/forehead with nasal congestion

res_headache_emergency.title: 🚨 CRITICAL HEADACHE EMERGENCY
res_headache_emergency.message: ⚠️ Sudden severe 'thunderclap' headache or headache with stiff neck/fever can indicate a brain bleed or meningitis!
guidance: Call 112 (or local emergency medical services) immediately.
Keep the person lying down in a quiet, dark, and calm environment.
Do not give any pain medication, food, or drinks until evaluated by paramedics.
Monitor responsiveness, alertness, and breathing closely.

res_headache_migraine.title: ⚠️ MIGRAINE HEADACHE GUIDANCE
res_headache_migraine.message: Pulsating pain usually on one side of head, often with light sensitivity or nausea.
res_headache_migraine.warning: Migraines can be debilitating. Rest in a dark, quiet room.
guidance: Rest in a quiet, dark, well-ventilated room with eyes closed.
Apply a cool damp cloth or cold compress across your forehead or back of neck.
Sip water slowly to stay hydrated.
If prescribed, take migraine relief medication early during the attack.
Avoid bright screens, loud noises, and strong odors.

res_headache_tension.title: 📋 TENSION HEADACHE FIRST-AID
res_headache_tension.message: Dull pressure on both sides of head or back of neck.
res_headache_tension.warning: Usually resolves with rest, relaxation, and hydration.
guidance: Apply a warm compress or heating pad to neck and shoulder muscles.
Perform gentle neck stretches and shoulder rolls.
Drink plenty of fresh water to ensure hydration.
Over-the-counter pain relievers (paracetamol/ibuprofen) may help if tolerated.
Take a break from computer screens and practice deep breathing.

res_headache_cluster.title: ⚠️ CLUSTER HEADACHE GUIDANCE
res_headache_cluster.message: Intense sharp pain around one eye with tearing or nasal congestion.
res_headache_cluster.warning: Requires medical evaluation for targeted treatment.
guidance: Sit upright in a comfortable chair—avoid lying down as it may worsen cluster pain.
Breathe deeply in fresh, cool air.
Apply a cool towel over the affected eye and temple.
Contact a doctor or specialist for high-flow oxygen or targeted prescription relief.

res_headache_sinus.title: 📋 SINUS HEADACHE GUIDANCE
res_headache_sinus.message: Facial pain and pressure from sinus congestion.
res_headache_sinus.warning: Consult doctor if pain lasts over 10 days or is accompanied by high fever.
guidance: Inhale warm steam from a hot shower or bowl of warm water.
Apply warm moist compresses around nose, cheeks, and forehead.
Use saline nasal spray to clear congestion.
Stay hydrated with warm fluids like tea or clear broth.

q_vomit_type.question: What best describes the vomiting or nausea symptoms?

options.label: Vomiting blood or dark 'coffee-ground' material, or severe abdominal pain
Inability to keep liquids down for 24+ hrs, signs of severe dehydration, or high fever
Sudden nausea after eating suspect food (suspected food poisoning)
Mild nausea, motion sickness, or morning sickness

res_vomiting_emergency.title: 🚨 GASTROINTESTINAL BLEEDING / VOMITING EMERGENCY
res_vomiting_emergency.message: ⚠️ Vomiting blood or coffee-ground material indicates internal GI bleeding!
guidance: Call 112 immediately for emergency medical assistance.
Keep the person sitting upright or leaning forward to prevent aspiration into lungs.
Do NOT give anything to eat or drink.
Monitor breathing, pulse, and mental alertness continuously.

res_vomiting_urgent.title: ⚠️ SEVERE DEHYDRATION / PERSISTENT VOMITING ALERT
res_vomiting_urgent.message: Inability to retain fluids or signs of severe dehydration (dark urine, sunken eyes, dry mouth).
res_vomiting_urgent.warning: Requires urgent medical care or IV rehydration.
guidance: Sip small amounts (teaspoonfuls) of Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) or electrolyte water every 5-10 minutes.
Do not try to drink large quantities of liquid all at once.
Seek urgent care or hospital evaluation for IV fluid replacement.

res_vomiting_food_poisoning.title: 📋 FOOD POISONING / ACUTE GASTROENTERITIS GUIDANCE
res_vomiting_food_poisoning.message: Nausea, vomiting, or stomach cramps following food intake.
res_vomiting_food_poisoning.warning: Stay hydrated and rest your stomach.
guidance: Rest your stomach for 1-2 hours after vomiting.
Sip small amounts of clear fluids (ORS, diluted apple juice, clear broth).
Gradually reintroduce bland foods (BRAT diet: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast).
Avoid fatty, spicy, sugary, or dairy foods until completely recovered.

res_vomiting_mild.title: 📋 MILD NAUSEA & MOTION SICKNESS FIRST-AID
res_vomiting_mild.message: Mild nausea, travel sickness, or indigestion.
guidance: Sip ginger tea, peppermint tea, or cold water slowly.
Sit upright in a well-ventilated area with fresh air.
Apply light pressure to the P6 acupressure point (3 finger-widths above inside wrist joint).
Rest quietly and avoid strong odors.

options.label: Fever with stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, or purple/red rash
High fever (>103°F / 39.4°C) or fever lasting more than 3 days
Fever with cough, sore throat, or body aches
Mild fever (<101°F / 38.3°C) with no severe symptoms

res_fever_emergency.title: 🚨 FEVER RED-FLAG EMERGENCY
res_fever_emergency.message: ⚠️ Fever accompanied by stiff neck, confusion, or unexplained rash can indicate meningitis or severe sepsis!
guidance: Call 112 immediately for emergency medical transport.
Keep the person resting in a comfortable position.
Do NOT submerge in ice water or rub with alcohol.
Monitor breathing, temperature, and responsiveness closely.

res_fever_high.title: ⚠️ HIGH / PROLONGED FEVER EVALUATION
res_fever_high.message: High body temperature or persistent fever.
res_fever_high.warning: Consult a healthcare provider for diagnosis and treatment.
guidance: Rest comfortably in a cool, well-ventilated room.
Drink plenty of water, broth, or electrolyte fluids to prevent dehydration.
Apply lukewarm (not cold) damp cloths to forehead and wrists.
Take fever-reducing medication (paracetamol/acetaminophen or ibuprofen) according to dosage instructions.
Visit a clinic or emergency doctor if fever does not come down.

res_fever_respiratory.title: 📋 FEVER WITH COLD / FLU SYMPTOMS
res_fever_respiratory.message: Fever with viral or upper respiratory symptoms.
res_fever_respiratory.warning: Monitor for chest pain or difficulty breathing.
guidance: Get plenty of bed rest to help your body fight infection.
Stay well-hydrated with water, warm tea, and soups.
Use paracetamol/ibuprofen as directed to reduce fever and body aches.
Seek medical care if breathing becomes difficult or cough worsens significantly.

res_fever_mild.title: 📋 MILD FEVER CARE
guidance: Rest in lightweight, breathable clothing.
Sip water frequently throughout the day.
Monitor temperature every 4-6 hours.
Contact doctor if fever persists past 3 days.

q_stomach_symptoms.question: What type of stomach or abdominal pain are you experiencing?

options.label: Severe pain starting near navel moving to lower right abdomen, with fever/vomiting
Sudden unbearable cramping pain radiating to back or groin (suspected stone)
Burning upper stomach pain, acid indigestion, or fullness
Mild bloating, gas, or mild menstrual cramps

res_abdominal_emergency.title: 🚨 SUSPECTED APPENDICITIS / ACUTE ABDOMEN
res_abdominal_emergency.message: ⚠️ Severe lower right abdominal pain with fever or rigidity can be appendicitis!
res_abdominal_emergency.warning: Call 112 or go to the emergency room immediately.
guidance: Seek immediate emergency medical evaluation (112 / ER).
Do NOT eat, drink, or take laxatives/painkillers, as this can obscure diagnosis or complicate surgery.
Lie down in a comfortable position, drawn-up knees may reduce belly tension.

res_abdominal_urgent.title: ⚠️ SEVERE RADIATING ABDOMINAL PAIN ALERT
res_abdominal_urgent.message: Intense cramping pain potentially caused by kidney stones or gallbladder issues.
guidance: Rest quietly and avoid solid food.
Have someone transport you to an urgent care clinic or hospital emergency room.
Seek emergency care if pain becomes unbearable, or accompanied by high fever or vomiting.

res_abdominal_gastritis.title: 📋 BURNING STOMACH / GASTRITIS FIRST-AID
res_abdominal_gastritis.message: Upper abdominal burning or acid reflux discomfort.
res_abdominal_gastritis.warning: Avoid trigger foods and lie down with head elevated.
guidance: Avoid spicy, acidic, fatty foods, coffee, and alcohol.
Sip small amounts of warm water or chamomile tea.
Over-the-counter antacids may provide temporary relief.
Rest with your upper body slightly elevated.

res_abdominal_mild.title: 📋 MILD INDIGESTION & BLOATING CARE
res_abdominal_mild.message: Mild stomach cramping or gas discomfort.
guidance: Apply a warm heating pad or hot water bottle to your abdomen.
Drink warm peppermint or chamomile tea.
Take gentle short walks to ease gas pressure.
Consult doctor if pain lasts more than 24-48 hours.

options.label: Dizziness with facial drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty (FAST stroke signs)
Room spinning sensation (vertigo) when moving head
Lightheadedness when standing up quickly or from dehydration

res_dizzy_stroke_emergency.title: 🚨 SUSPECTED STROKE EMERGENCY
res_dizzy_stroke_emergency.message: ⚠️ Dizziness with sudden weakness, numbness, facial drooping, or speech trouble is a STROKE EMERGENCY!
guidance: Call 112 immediately—every minute counts for stroke treatment.
Lay the person down flat with head slightly raised.
Note the exact time symptoms started.
Do NOT give any food, drink, or aspirin.

res_dizzy_vertigo.title: 📋 VERTIGO (SPINNING SENSATION) GUIDANCE
res_dizzy_vertigo.message: Room spinning or balance disturbance, often inner-ear related.
res_dizzy_vertigo.warning: Sit or lie down immediately to prevent falls.
guidance: Sit or lie flat immediately on a stable surface.
Keep your head still and focus on a fixed point in front of you.
Avoid sudden posture changes, bright lights, or reading.
See an ENT doctor or physician if vertigo persists.

res_dizzy_lightheaded.title: 📋 LIGHTHEADEDNESS & DEHYDRATION CARE
res_dizzy_lightheaded.message: Feeling faint or lightheaded upon standing or from heat.
guidance: Sit down immediately or lie flat with legs slightly elevated.
Sip water or electrolyte fluids slowly.
Rest in a cool, well-ventilated area.
Stand up very slowly when feeling better.

q_hand_location.question: Where exactly is the hand or arm pain located?

q_left_hand_finger.question: Which specific finger or area of your hand/arm is affected?

options.label: Entire arm or hand (Not specific to one finger)

q_finger_symptoms.question: What kind of symptoms or pain are you experiencing in your finger/hand?

options.label: Sudden injury, fall, cut, or finger jam
Swollen joint, redness, or throbbing pain
Accompanied by chest pressure, shortness of breath, or sweating

q_finger_numbness_type.question: Which specific finger(s) feel numb or tingling?

q_hand_onset.question: Did the hand/arm pain start suddenly (e.g., after an injury/fall) or develop gradually?

options.label: Sudden pain after trauma, fall, or impact
Sudden onset without any physical injury
Gradual onset over days or weeks

q_hand_deformity.question: Is there any visible bone deformity, open wound, bone sticking out, or severe swelling?

options.label: Yes - bone protruding through skin or severe bleeding
Yes - visibly bent/deformed bone or unable to move fingers
No - just swelling, bruising, or mild pain when moving

q_hand_cardiac_check.question: Are you also experiencing chest pain, chest tightness, shortness of breath, sweating, or dizziness?

options.label: Yes - chest pain, breathlessness, or sweating
No - pain is only in the hand/arm

q_hand_character.question: How would you describe the feeling of the pain?

options.label: Numbness, tingling, or 'pins and needles' down arm/fingers
Throbbing, redness, heat, or swollen joint
Dull ache, stiffness after repetitive computer work or lifting

res_hand_cardiac_emergency.title: 🚨 CRITICAL CARDIAC EMERGENCY WARNING
res_hand_cardiac_emergency.message: ⚠️ Sudden left/right arm pain accompanied by chest tightness, breathlessness, or sweating can be a sign of a HEART ATTACK!
guidance: Call emergency services (112) immediately.
Stop all physical activity and sit down in a comfortable position.
Loosen tight clothing around neck and chest.
Do NOT attempt to drive yourself to the hospital.
Monitor breathing and responsiveness closely.

res_hand_open_fracture_emergency.title: 🚨 OPEN FRACTURE / SEVERE TRAUMA EMERGENCY
res_hand_open_fracture_emergency.message: ⚠️ Bone protruding through skin or severe uncontrolled bleeding!
res_hand_open_fracture_emergency.warning: Call 112 immediately for emergency medical transport.
guidance: Call 112 immediately.
Control bleeding by applying pressure around the wound (do not press on protruding bone).
Do NOT try to push the bone back in or straighten the arm/hand.
Cover wound loosely with a sterile bandage or clean cloth.
Keep arm immobilized until paramedics arrive.

res_hand_closed_fracture_urgent.title: ⚠️ SUSPECTED FRACTURE / DISLOCATION EVALUATION
res_hand_closed_fracture_urgent.message: Deformed bone, severe pain, or inability to move hand/fingers following impact.
res_hand_closed_fracture_urgent.warning: Requires urgent hospital X-ray and splinting.
guidance: Immobilize the arm and hand using a sling or soft pillow padding.
Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth to reduce swelling (15 mins on/off).
Do NOT attempt to force or bend the fingers/wrist back into place.
Visit an urgent care center or emergency department immediately.

res_hand_nerve_urgent.title: ⚠️ NERVE IRRITATION / CARPAL TUNNEL EVALUATION
res_hand_nerve_urgent.message: Numbness, tingling, or shooting nerve pain down arm or into thumb/fingers.
res_hand_nerve_urgent.warning: Consult a doctor for neurological and orthopedic examination.
guidance: Rest hand and arm in a neutral position; avoid bending wrist sharply.
Avoid repetitive gripping, typing, or heavy lifting.
Wear a supportive wrist splint if available, especially at night.
Schedule an appointment with a doctor if numbness or weakness persists.

res_hand_inflammation_guidance.title: 📋 JOINT INFLAMMATION / TENDONITIS CARE
res_hand_inflammation_guidance.message: Throbbing pain, joint swelling, or redness in wrist or fingers.
guidance: Rest the affected hand/wrist and avoid activities that trigger pain.
Apply a cold compress wrapped in a towel for 15-20 minutes 3 times a day.
Elevate hand on a pillow above heart level to reduce swelling.
Over-the-counter anti-inflammatory meds (ibuprofen) may help if tolerated.

res_hand_sprain_care.title: 📋 HAND / WRIST SPRAIN FIRST-AID (R.I.C.E.)
res_hand_sprain_care.message: Mild swelling or strain following minor twist or bump.
res_hand_sprain_care.warning: Follow R.I.C.E. protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
guidance: Rest: Avoid using the injured hand/wrist for heavy tasks.
Ice: Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15 minutes at a time.
Compression: Wrap wrist/hand lightly with an elastic bandage (not too tight).
Elevation: Prop hand up on pillows when sitting or resting.

res_hand_strain_low.title: 📋 MUSCLE STRAIN / REPETITIVE STRAIN FIRST-AID
res_hand_strain_low.message: Dull ache or fatigue from typing, gaming, or overuse.
guidance: Take regular 5-minute breaks every 30 minutes from computer or manual work.
Perform gentle finger, wrist, and forearm stretches.
Apply warm compress to tight muscles after acute stage.
Ensure ergonomic keyboard and mouse positioning.

res_carpal_tunnel_guidance.title: 📋 THUMB / INDEX / MIDDLE FINGER CARPAL TUNNEL GUIDANCE
res_carpal_tunnel_guidance.message: Numbness, tingling, or pain in the thumb, index, or middle finger often indicates median nerve compression (Carpal Tunnel Syndrome).
res_carpal_tunnel_guidance.warning: Avoid prolonged wrist flexion, repetitive typing, or heavy gripping.
guidance: Rest the hand and keep the wrist in a neutral, straight position.
Wear a supportive wrist splint (especially at night) to prevent nerve pinching.
Take regular ergonomic breaks during computer or manual work.
Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for 10-15 minutes if swelling is present.
Consult a doctor or neurologist if numbness or thumb weakness persists.

res_ulnar_nerve_guidance.title: 📋 LITTLE FINGER & RING FINGER ULNAR NERVE GUIDANCE
res_ulnar_nerve_guidance.message: Numbness, tingling, or pain in the little finger (pinky) and ring finger is commonly caused by ulnar nerve compression at the elbow.
res_ulnar_nerve_guidance.warning: Avoid leaning on your elbows or bending your arms sharply for long periods.
guidance: Avoid resting your elbows on hard desks or armrests.
Keep your arm straighter when sleeping or holding a phone.
Avoid tight elbow sleeves or excessive elbow bending.
Perform gentle nerve glide exercises to relieve tension.
Schedule a physician evaluation if numbness, tingling, or weak grip continues.

q_leg_type.question: What type of leg or foot pain are you experiencing?

options.label: Severe sudden pain / Inability to stand
Cut, open wound, or severe bleeding
Deep leg swelling with redness and warmth

q_leg_trauma.question: Was this caused by a severe fall, accident, or heavy impact?

q_leg_weight.question: Are you able to put weight or walk on the affected leg?

options.label: No - completely unable to bear weight

res_leg_emergency.title: 🚨 URGENT MEDICAL EVALUATION REQUIRED
res_leg_emergency.message: ⚠️ Severe leg trauma, suspected fracture, or deep vein thrombosis (DVT) red flags detected.
res_leg_emergency.warning: Inability to bear weight after trauma or sudden severe swelling with warmth/redness requires emergency medical examination.
guidance: Call emergency services (112) or go to the nearest Emergency Department.
Do NOT try to walk or force weight onto the injured leg.
Immobilize the leg in the position found; do not try to straighten or snap bones back.
If bleeding is present, apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth.
Keep the person calm, warm, and resting comfortably.

res_leg_urgent.title: ⚠️ SPRAIN / STRAIN FIRST-AID GUIDANCE
res_leg_urgent.message: Significant leg/ankle sprain or muscle strain.
res_leg_urgent.warning: Rest the leg immediately to prevent further ligament or tissue damage.
guidance: Rest: Avoid putting weight on the injured leg or ankle.
Ice: Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 15-20 minutes every 2-3 hours.
Compression: Wrap with an elastic bandage snugly (not too tight).
Elevation: Prop the leg up above heart level using pillows.
If swelling worsens or you cannot stand after 24 hours, visit an urgent care medical clinic.

res_leg_low.title: 📋 MUSCLE CRAMP & MILD STRAIN FIRST AID
res_leg_low.message: Mild muscle soreness or leg cramp.
res_leg_low.warning: Monitor symptoms. Stay hydrated and avoid over-exertion.
guidance: Gently stretch and massage the calf or thigh muscle.
Drink plenty of water or electrolyte solution.
Apply warm compress to tight muscles after any acute swelling subsides.
Rest the leg in a comfortable position.

res_leg_wound.title: ⚠️ LEG CUT & WOUND CARE
res_leg_wound.message: Leg cut or laceration requiring first-aid.
res_leg_wound.warning: Ensure bleeding is controlled and keep the wound clean to prevent infection.
guidance: Apply firm, continuous direct pressure using a clean towel or gauze.
Elevate the leg above the heart while applying pressure.
Rinse wound gently with clean water once bleeding stops.
Apply sterile bandage; seek medical attention if deep or requires stitches.

q_back_trauma.question: Did a recent high-impact fall, motor vehicle collision, or trauma cause this back/joint pain?

options.label: No - routine movement or gradual onset

q_back_symptoms.question: Are you experiencing any of these neurological symptoms?

options.label: Numbness or weakness in legs / arms
Loss of bowel or bladder control
Stiffness or dull muscle ache only

res_back_emergency.title: 🚨 POTENTIAL SPINAL EMERGENCY WARNING
res_back_emergency.message: ⚠️ Neurological deficits or severe spinal trauma red flags detected.
res_back_emergency.warning: Back trauma or loss of sensation/control can indicate nerve compression or spinal cord injury. Seek immediate emergency care.
guidance: Call emergency services (112) immediately.
Keep the person completely still; do NOT move their head, neck, or back.
Do not allow the person to stand or twist.
Keep the person warm and calm until paramedics arrive.

res_back_urgent.title: ⚠️ URGENT JOINT / BACK EVALUATION
res_back_urgent.message: Joint swelling, severe pain, or fever detected.
res_back_urgent.warning: A hot, swollen joint or severe back pain with fever requires prompt medical diagnosis.
guidance: Rest the affected joint in a supported position.
Apply cold packs for acute joint swelling (15-20 mins).
Consult an urgent care physician promptly.

res_back_low.title: 📋 BACK & JOINT CARE GUIDANCE
res_back_low.message: Mild back strain or joint stiffness.
res_back_low.warning: Maintain gentle posture and avoid heavy lifting.
guidance: Rest in a comfortable position (e.g. lying flat with pillows under knees).
Apply mild heat or ice to the affected muscle area.
Avoid bending or lifting heavy objects.
Perform gentle walking as tolerated.
